# Ivan de Murard, Product Builder

## Identity

Homepage statement: "Product builder. Agentic AI systems for operations." Currently building an architecture of specialised agents for hotel operations.

Ivan de Murard is a product builder based in Paris, France. He has five years of product management experience across start-ups, scale-ups and large groups, plus two years as co-founder and product lead of Sonor, a B2G SaaS for urban noise mapping. He designs from operational experience, ships with AI, and keeps the human at the center.

Contact: ivandemurard@gmail.com. Booking: https://cal.com/ivandemurard/discussion-and-introduction. LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/ivandemurard/. GitHub: https://github.com/IvandeMurard.

## Convictions

1. Human interactions first. Technology should give time back to people, not pull them deeper into screens. The best automation is the one that lets a host be more present.
2. Real business value. Reducing operational costs, freeing capacity, sharpening decisions. Every product has to move a number that matters to the business.
3. Full-stack 0 to 1 craft. From insight to shipped product, bridging digital interfaces and physical operations, so the experience holds together end to end.

## How he works

1. Reading the ground. Field-level fluency in operations: boutique hotels, F&B, design partners, open-data ecosystems. He learns an environment before he designs for it.
2. From insight to product decisions. Aetherix is the proof: a real operating layer for boutique hotels, not a slideware concept.
3. Right tool for the problem. Sometimes a workflow, sometimes a checklist, sometimes an agentic system. The lightest mechanism that solves the job, with the human in the loop.

## Aetherix

URL: https://ivandemurard.com/aetherix. Meta-repo (public): https://github.com/IvandeMurard/hospitality-agentic-mesh.

Aetherix, the F&B execution agent for boutique hotels. Tomorrow's covers, a staffing grid that fits, and less waste: one message a day, in WhatsApp, with the reasoning attached. Three promises with honesty labels: tomorrow's covers (shipped, in pilot), staffing that fits (pilot hypothesis), less waste (target outcome); two of the three are pilot hypotheses, not measured results. Thesis: understand like a human (contextual reasoning grounded in each property's history), measure like a machine (every recommendation stored next to its real outcome), learn like a network (per-property memory today, federated priors next). Vision, four nodes with honest status: Aetherix the F&B agent (Built), Tacet the environmental-signal node (Prototype), Anima the Guest Cognition agent (Design), Orchestrator the supervisory agent (Stub). Operational memory is the mechanism that makes the forecast specific to one property, not the offer. Cycle: Memory, Prediction, Action, Learning. Delivered on WhatsApp. MCP-native, callable by any other agent in the stack. Status: Phase 3, Pilot. Staging live on Fly.io (Paris). Apaleo OAuth and MCP read access operational. MCP Server v0 is live. Design partner pilot starting. Contrast with Lore: Lore shares this architecture and cannot close the same loop, nothing there tells the system whether an observation was right; Aetherix has an outcome to compare against.

The loop that learns. Every day the same loop deposits one more grain of calibrated experience into the property's operational memory. Memory recalls what worked here. Prediction proposes tomorrow's covers, staffing, waste risk with drivers. Action lands as one WhatsApp message with one-tap accept, modify or reject. Learning records every reply as feedback; the pilot tests whether it improves future recommendations. Day 7 is cold-start, honest confidence, leans on generic cross-property context patterns and the first week of local signals. Day 90 is the expected, not measured, state: drivers become property-specific, calibrated by enough Tuesdays, events and overrides to fit this exact place. Caveat: a true federated cohort prior (HiveMemory) is research, Phase 4 and beyond, anonymized aggregates only, no cross-tenant raw data, ever. Measured gains begin with the live pilot, not the synthetic baseline.

Problem. In hospitality, the people who know how the property really runs carry that knowledge in their heads. When a manager leaves, the property starts again from scratch. Combined with the inherent complexity of F&B operations (multiple outlets, mixed guest segments, volatile demand, labor shortages), this creates chronic inefficiencies. The underlying bottleneck is not data, it is synthesis: combining internal context (occupancy, capture rates, POS history) with external signals (weather, local events) into a recommendation calibrated to this property. Aetherix builds that synthesis automatically, learns from manager feedback, and delivers it where managers already are. Glue, not replacement.

The Mesh. Aetherix is one node in a network of specialized, MCP-native agents. Each node owns a strict bounded context and communicates only through MCP. Nodes: Aetherix (F&B execution: forecast, staffing, memory, receipts, Live staging), Tacet (Sensory: weather, noise, open data, risk, Phase 3), Orchestrator (Supervisory: MCP routing, business rules, Phase 3 stub, dedicated repo Phase 4), Anima (Guest Cognition Layer, synthetic PoC at the Anthropic hackathon Jun 2026, production DPIA-gated). Aetherix ↔ Tacet: Aetherix owns internal context, Tacet owns external context, the Orchestrator calls both. Together they form one predictive twin.

Architecture, push-first pipeline. Apaleo (OAuth2 and MCP read) + Open-Meteo + PredictHQ → Prophet forecast and staffing → pgvector memory recall (OperationalMemory + HiveMemory cold-start, research) → Claude Sonnet reasoning (Gemini/GPT fallback) → WhatsApp or Email. MCP Server v0 live on Fly.io (Paris), three atomic tools, multi-tenant. Stack: FastAPI, Python 3.12, Prophet, pgvector (Mistral 1024d, HNSW), Claude Sonnet (Gemini/GPT fallback), Redis (Upstash), Supabase (PostgreSQL, RLS, EU), Fly.io (Paris).

Built to be trusted. Evaluation as a contract (Qonto-inspired): versioned golden datasets, hard CI gate. Observability and metering: every MCP tool call is one structured event, auditable, queryable, priceable. Multi-tenant security: hotel_id scoped at every layer (RLS, Python guards, MCP token binding), resolved server-side, never a tool input. Read-only PMS access. GDPR: Supabase EU, HiveMemory is anonymized aggregates only.

What remains private. The project includes proprietary research on cross-domain operational context and cold-start learning. Public materials focus on the engineering evidence: evaluation gates, traceability, safety guardrails, privacy boundaries, and outcome measurement.

Where we are, honestly. Phase 3 · Pilot, design partner starting, real-world measurement begins now. Target labor cost variance: −3% to −8% over 90 days on a live property (target, not measured yet). Security: 14/14 gates passing. Calibration baseline (synthetic backtest, not a headline): MAPE 15.09% on J+1 covers, 22% gate PASS. Real-world MAPE begins with the pilot.

Roadmap. Phase 0 Validation done · Phase 1 Observability done · Phase 2 Receipts done · Phase 3 Pilot current · Phase 4 Scale planned (Mews, POS, Federated HiveMemory, Context Graph, Anima) · Phase 5 Vision planned (Revenue Orchestrator).

Anima, sister node. Guest Cognition Layer PoC shipped at Anthropic hackathon Jun 2026. 4-layer temporal memory (working, episodic, semantic, segment) with confidence-weighted claims. Production is Phase 4, DPIA-gated.

Role and model. Solo architect and builder. Pricing: Results-as-a-Service, outcome-based.

## Tacet

URL: https://ivandemurard.com/tacet. Tacet is a headless Environmental Twin for hospitality (B2B, 2026, V3). It began as a Bruitparif-powered Score Sérénité dashboard for Parisians, then pivoted to a physics-based, software-only model of the property and its surroundings, exposed via an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server. Four architectural pillars: (A) a 3D ray-tracing physics engine built on shapely and osmnx that computes line of sight and building shielding to cut false positives; (B) a dual memory store with idiosyncratic learning per GPS coordinate plus a Hive Mind that recalibrates baseline sensitivity across the network; (C) a human-in-the-loop guardrail that never changes prices on its own but formulates Price Modifier Rules (for example minus 15% on street-facing suites between June 12 and 14) for Revenue Manager approval; (D) conversational explainability through a mathematical Chain of Thought embedded in every JSON payload (base noise, distance attenuation, ray-tracing penalty, final impact). Stack: Python 3.12, FastAPI, Anthropic MCP SDK, SQLAlchemy, OSMnx, Shapely, GeoPandas, OAuth2, Mews Open API, Apaleo API, RMS webhooks. Designed to work in tandem with Aetherix: Aetherix consumes Tacet rules via MCP, providing internal context (occupancy, F&B, staffing) while Tacet provides external context (street, weather, events). Together they form one predictive twin. ESG impact: yield protection through pre-emptive pricing of noisy inventory, operational excellence through F&B and staffing buffers ahead of weather or social disruption, sustainability through proactive HVAC optimisation and noise mitigation. Source: https://github.com/IvandeMurard/tacet-app/blob/main/CASE_STUDY_V3.md.

## Lore

URL: https://ivandemurard.com/lore. Repository: https://github.com/IvandeMurard/Lore (tag v0.1-hackathon for the V1 build).

Lore is a voice AI mentor for aviation maintenance: a living memory for a trade that is handed down out loud. It captures what a retiring technician knows and never wrote down, then gives it back to a junior on the shop floor by voice. Origin: Speechmatics x AI Collective Paris hackathon, 28 Feb to 1 Mar 2026, V1 built in 24 hours by a team of four, developed solo since. Status: prototype, synthetic procedures, mock aircraft data, evaluation harness running in CI.

Three modes. Capture: the senior debriefs by voice after an intervention and Lore interviews back, filing knowledge against airframe, component and conditions. Query: the junior asks out loud and the answer arrives in three layers, in order, the relevant SOP excerpt, then the senior's oral knowledge attributed by name and month, then that specific aircraft's own history. Log: spoken work records go straight into the aircraft's memory, no keyboard.

Rule number one: Lore never contradicts a procedure, it completes it. Where a senior's habit and the manual disagree, the manual sets the limit and the senior's judgement is reported as context, attributed.

Thesis. Aetherix exists because hotels lose critical knowledge when a manager leaves; Lore exists because the same loss happens when a senior technician retires. What separates them is the cost of being wrong: in hospitality it compounds quietly, in maintenance a wrong figure touches airworthiness on the first occurrence.

Stack: Speechmatics real-time STT, OpenAI GPT-4o, Backboard (thread per aircraft and per technician), OpenAI TTS, Next.js 14, TypeScript, Tailwind, Vercel.

## Anima

URL: https://ivandemurard.com/anima. The guest node of the Hospitality Agentic Mesh, and the node that is not allowed to simply accumulate. It is a memory product with a deliberate limit, not a personalisation product.

Lineage. Digital twins started with assets, and hospitality mostly stopped there (predictive maintenance, refurbishment simulation, energy). The interesting extension is toward people: research on human-centered digital twins in hospitality (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13078991/) models the employee, and its design rule is that such a system supports human judgement rather than replacing it. That paper is a study of adoption intent across 141 hotel employees, not a deployed system. Anima applies the same shift to the guest relationship, and the two are not symmetrical: an employee can be told they are modelled, consulted and can refuse; a guest cannot meaningfully consent to being modelled during a two-night stay. The older version of this was the concierge who never had to ask twice, a twin with a bus factor of one, which is the same loss Lore addresses for technical expertise.

Four memory layers with different lifetimes. Working: the current stay, expires at check-out. Episodic: this stay and a short tail, weeks. Semantic: durable preferences stated or repeatedly confirmed, long with decay. Segment: anonymised patterns, aggregate and never individual. Temporal separation is the design: a guest ordering a decaf at 11pm before an early flight should be used tonight and never become a permanent belief.

Confidence. Nothing is stored as a fact. Every claim carries a weight, a source and an age, and weights fall unless renewed. A preference from 2019 nobody has confirmed does not outvote something said last week. A system that reports a confidence it did not measure is worse than one that reports none.

Ethics in the data model. Edmondo Grassi (The Remains of the Stay: Memory, Identity, and the Afterlife of the Guest, Hotel Yearbook 2026 Technology Edition) notes that the stay no longer ends at check-out, it merely changes form, and asks whether remembering is an act of care or an exercise of power. The answer here is decay on every claim, layers that expire by design, inference marked as inference, and a scope gate that makes total recall impossible rather than discouraged.

Boundaries. Any consumer declares which layer it queries; there is no call returning everything known about a person. Anima answers who a guest is right now and never what to do about it: that belongs to the orchestrator, with a human validating. Guest experience is not a node, it is a cross-cutting signal, which is why guest.* lives in the shared contract.

Status. Synthetic proof of concept. Four-layer memory implemented, working MCP server, evaluated on a synthetic cohort. Never run on a real guest, and it will not until a formal data-protection assessment is complete. Shipped as a prototype at an Anthropic hackathon, June 2026. Production is phase 4.

## Field Notes

Index: https://ivandemurard.com/journal.

- Harnesses, graders, closed loops (2026-07-31). URL: https://ivandemurard.com/journal/harnesses-graders-closed-loops. A working vocabulary for building evaluation into AI products from day one: case set, grader, harness, protocol, open loop, closed loop. Covers the three arms of evaluation, "working" against "reliable" across five dimensions, the reliability pyramid, evaluation as a contract, acceptance criteria and tiered severity, confidence, human in the loop by design or by default, and what a harness finds that no unit test sees. Tested on Aetherix and Lore.
- A hard call on Aetherix's agent boundaries (2026-04-20). URL: https://ivandemurard.com/journal/agent-boundaries-aetherix. On where to draw the line between forecasting and acting, and why splitting Prophet from Claude shaped the rest of the architecture.

## Frequently asked questions

Q: Who is Ivan de Murard?
A: A Paris-based product builder with five years across start-ups, scale-ups and large groups, plus two years co-founding Sonor. He focuses on product management, service design, and agentic AI for operations.

Q: What is Aetherix?
A: A food & beverage execution agent for hotels. It tells a manager how many covers to expect, how to staff for them, and how to cut food waste. Used by other agents via MCP or by a hotel / F&B manager with WhatsApp. Currently pilot testing in the hospitality agentic mesh.

Q: What is Lore?
A: A voice AI mentor that captures, qualifies, and leverages the tacit expertise from senior to junior collaborators. Just ask. Used by a junior technician on the shop floor, hands busy. Prototype, built at a Speechmatics hackathon in early 2026.

Q: How can I reach him?
A: Email ivandemurard@gmail.com or book a call at https://cal.com/ivandemurard/discussion-and-introduction.
